text: ivy: Heads up — several deep links into the onboarding guide are landing at the top of the page instead of their target headings. Customer reported it: https://docs.redwood.ai/onboarding#env-setup oscar: can you paste the heading and any nearby HTML? sometimes leftover or inline attrs create weird ids. ivy: snippet from the page: ```md ### Env setup — OS-specific notes We recommend... > Note: use the venv command on linux/mac ``` rachel: ah — explicit id on the plus the heading slug collide. Browser jumps to the first matching id (the span). That explains the behavior. ioscar: quick options: 1) remove the id on the span, 2) move the note under the heading so it isn't before the heading, or 3) add an explicit safe id on the heading and update links. ivy: i prefer option 3 as it's least invasive for the content. i'll add `{#env-setup}` to the heading and remove the id from the span to avoid duplicate. also want to add a tiny link-sanity check to CI to fail PRs that introduce duplicate ids. rachel: good. maybe we should also add a small `scripts/slug_sanitize.py` that normalizes heading text -> slug using the same logic as the renderer, then run it in CI to detect collisions early. ioscar: opened tiny PR with changes and a new GH action: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4012 Patch includes: ```diff - -> Note: use the venv command on linux/mac - +> Note: use the venv command on linux/mac + +### Env setup \u2014 OS-specific notes {#env-setup} ``` and adds `.github/workflows/docs-slug-check.yml` which runs `python scripts/slug_sanitize.py --check` on changed markdown files. ci-bot: Running docs slug-sanity check for PR #4012... docslint-bot: slug_sanitize found 0 collisions and 0 non-ascii codepoints in changed files. ci-bot: mkdocs build --strict; yarn docs:linkcheck running... ioscar: PTAL @rachel. I kept the note above the heading but removed the html id so the page flow is unchanged. explicit heading id prevents accidental mismatch. rachel: LGTM. CI green. Merging now. commit: f2e7b12 ivy: thanks! follow-up: i'll schedule a repo-wide run of slug_sanitize and open PRs for any pages that show duplicates. also adding a CONTRIBUTING note: "prefer explicit heading ids for sections that are linked from external content". ioscar: also leaving a comment in the quickstart that links to the new slug-check GH action so external contributors see it. iv: closing the loop — if anyone spots odd deep links, please drop them here. :rocket:
